title: The Gift-Wrap Trial
covers: finding the surface area of rectangular prisms and triangular prisms by adding every face, including opposite matching pairs
cert: finding the surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms

intro.caption: Lesson 5-7 — surface area of prisms. Cubeland Court is in session! Dree claimed one sheet of gift wrap would cover the whole prize box, and half the box is still bare.

balloons.t: Your Honor! Dree bought ONE sheet of wrap for a huge box. Half the sides are naked!
Order in the court! Also, did anyone bring snacks?
I saw three numbers—length, width, height—so I multiplied three pairs and stopped!
A box has SIX faces, Dree! Every face has an opposite twin, so you forgot to double them!

pages.caption: A rectangular prism has 3 pairs of congruent opposite faces: top and bottom, front and back, left and right.

balloons.t: Check Exhibit A: a 10 × 6 × 4 box. Count all six faces, not just three!
Exhibit B is a triangular prism! Two triangle ends plus three rectangle sides.
Five faces total. Find each face area and add all five together!
Our math is flawless! For a 12 × 7 × 5 prism, we got 323 cm².
Wait—even I can spot that! You forgot to double the last pair!

pages.ch: Boss Gate · Rule on the Wrap

balloons.t: Final ruling! How much wrap does the 14 × 10 × 6 prize box really need?
One sheet covers 400 in². Let's prove the exact surface area!
Case closed! Two sheets of wrap, all six faces covered!

win.caption: To find the surface area of any prism, find the area of every face—including both faces in each matching pair—and add them together in square units.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Check Exhibit A
gates.prompt: Find the surface area of Exhibit A (10 in × 6 in × 4 in) and spot Dree's missing step.
hints: Conceptual: a rectangular prism has 6 faces in 3 congruent pairs.
Procedural: compute lw, lh, and wh, multiply each by 2, and add the three products.

worked.q: What is the surface area of an 8 × 5 × 3 box?

items.label: Exhibit A is 10 in × 6 in × 4 in. Total surface area (in²):
items.aria: surface area of 10 by 6 by 4 rectangular prism in square inches

fb.msg: 124 is only 3 faces (60 + 40 + 24). Every face has a matching twin—multiply by 2!
240 is 10 × 6 × 4, which is volume. Surface area adds all 6 faces.
You left out the 6 × 4 pair (2 × 24 = 48). Include all three pairs.

items.q: Dree got 124 in² for the 10 × 6 × 4 box. What mistake did Dree make?

options.t: Forgot to double each face area for the opposite matching face
Multiplied length × width × height instead of adding
Subtracted the bottom face from the total
options.fb: Even subtracting one face would leave 5 faces, not 3.

gates.pass: 248 in²! Every single face of Exhibit A is accounted for.

gates.title: Gate 2 · The Wedge Exhibit
gates.prompt: Exhibit B is a triangular prism. Find the area of its 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.
hints: Conceptual: a triangular prism has 5 faces—2 congruent triangles and 3 rectangles.
Procedural: find two triangles with 2 × (½ × base × height), then add the 3 rectangles (each side × prism length).

steps: Practice wedge: length 8 in; triangle base 4 in, height 3 in, sides 4, 5, 5 in.
Two triangles: 2 × (½ × 4 × 3) = 12 in². Three rectangles: (4 + 5 + 5) × 8 = 112 in².
worked.q: A triangular prism is 10 in long with triangle ends (base 8, height 6, sides 8, 6, 10). Total SA?

items.label: Exhibit B is 10 in long. Triangle ends: base 6 in, height 4 in, sides 6, 5, 5 in. Total SA (in²):
items.aria: surface area of triangular prism in square inches

fb.msg: 160 is only the 3 rectangles (60 + 50 + 50). Add the 2 triangle ends (24 in²).
172 only adds ONE triangle (12 in²). There are two triangle ends.
24 is just the two triangle ends. Don't forget the three rectangular sides!

items.q: How many faces does any triangular prism have?

options.fb: 6 faces is a rectangular prism. A triangle only has 3 sides, so only 3 rectangles wrap around it.
That leaves out one of the ends or sides. Count 2 triangles + 3 rectangles.

gates.pass: 184 in² and 5 faces! Moss places the painted wedge cleanly on the evidence rack.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Find the Missing Face
gates.prompt: The Champs wrote SA = 2(12 × 7) + 2(12 × 5) + (7 × 5) = 323 cm² for a 12 × 7 × 5 prism. Catch and fix their error.
hints: Conceptual: every one of the 3 face pairs must be multiplied by 2.
Procedural: look at the last term (7 × 5). They only counted it once instead of twice.

steps: Practice error: for a 9 × 4 × 3 prism, someone wrote 2(36) + 2(27) + 12 = 138 cm².
The last face (4 × 3 = 12) was not doubled, so 12 cm² is missing.
worked.q: For a 7 × 3 × 2 prism, someone wrote 2(21) + 2(14) + 6 = 76. What is the true SA?

items.label: In 2(12×7) + 2(12×5) + (7×5) = 323 cm², how many cm² are missing?
items.aria: missing square centimeters in Champs calculation

fb.msg: 70 is the whole pair (2 × 35). They already counted one 35, so only 35 is missing.
358 is the full correct surface area. This question asks how much is missing from 323.

items.fbDefault: They counted (7 × 5) once instead of twice. What is 7 × 5?

items.label: What is the true surface area of the 12 × 7 × 5 prism (cm²)?
items.aria: true surface area of 12 by 7 by 5 prism in square centimeters

fb.msg: 323 is The Champs' broken answer—it's missing the second 7 × 5 face.
179 is only 3 faces. Double all three pairs.

gates.pass: 35 cm² missing, true total 358 cm²! The Champs quickly hide their clipboard.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Rule on the Wrap
gates.prompt: Time for the final verdict on the 14 in × 10 in × 6 in prize box. One sheet of gift wrap covers 400 in².
hints: Conceptual: find the full surface area of all 6 faces first, then compare to 400 in² per sheet.
Procedural: compute 2(14×10) + 2(14×6) + 2(10×6), then see how many 400 in² sheets are needed to cover it.

steps: If one sheet covers 150 in², 1 sheet is not enough (202 > 150).
So 2 sheets are needed to cover the whole box.
worked.q: If a box has SA = 310 in² and one sheet covers 200 in², how many sheets do you need?

items.label: Verdict 1 · Prize box is 14 in × 10 in × 6 in. True surface area (in²):
items.aria: surface area of 14 by 10 by 6 prize box in square inches

fb.msg: 284 is Dree's half-box mistake! Double each of the three pairs.
840 is volume (14 × 10 × 6). Surface area adds all 6 outside faces.
You left out the 10 × 6 pair (2 × 60 = 120). Include all three pairs.

items.q: Verdict 2 · One sheet of gift wrap covers 400 in². How many sheets does Dree need for the 568 in² box?

options.t: 1 sheet, because 284 in² is under 400 in²
options.fb: 284 in² only covers 3 faces. The full box is 568 in², which is more than 400 in².

options.t: 2 sheets, because 1 sheet (400 in²) is too small and 2 sheets (800 in²) cover 568 in²

options.fb: 2 sheets give 800 in², which already covers 568 in² with paper to spare.

options.t: 1 sheet, if we skip the bottom face
options.fb: Even without one 140 in² face, 568 − 140 = 428 in², which is still over 400 in².

items.q: Verdict 3 · Why is surface area measured in square inches (in²) instead of cubic inches?

options.t: It measures flat 2D faces covering the outside
It measures how much space fits inside the box
options.fb: Space inside is volume (cubic units). Wrapping paper covers the flat outside.

options.t: It measures the total length of the edges
options.fb: Edge length uses plain inches, not square inches.

gates.pass: BANG! 568 in² takes 2 sheets of wrap! Judge Gel orders Dree to wrap the back of the box.

journal.heading: Lesson 5-7 — what the courtroom taught us
rows: Six faces in 3 matching pairs: SA = 2lw + 2lh + 2wh. Always double every pair.
Five faces total: 2 congruent triangle ends plus 3 rectangular lateral faces. Add all 5 areas.
Surface area covers flat outside faces, so answers always use square units (in², cm², ft²).
Finding lw + lh + wh only covers half the box. Opposite faces match, so every pair counts twice.
journal.quote: "Double every pair or half your present stays naked." — Gel

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 5-7 (Determine Surface Area of Prisms) as one focused read. Covers only this lesson: surface area of rectangular prisms (doubling all 3 face pairs) and triangular prisms (2 triangle bases + 3 lateral rectangles).
standards: Find the surface area of right rectangular prisms, right triangular prisms, and pyramids using nets
